explanation.text:
With a general strain of confidence, hope, and joy, especially in God's worship, in the midst of dangers, the Psalmist introduces prayer for divine help and guidance. (Psa 27:1-14)

light--is a common figure for comfort.

strength--or, "stronghold"--affording security against all violence. The interrogations give greater vividness to the negation implied.

bsb.title: Of David.
bsb.text: The LORD is my light and my salvation—whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life—whom shall I dread?

explanation.text:
eat . . . my flesh-- (Job 19:22; Psa 14:4). The allusion to wild beasts illustrates their rapacity.

they stumbled--"they" is emphatic; not I, but they were destroyed.

bsb.text: When the wicked came upon me to devour my flesh, my enemies and foes stumbled and fell.

explanation.text:
In the greatest dangers.

in this--that is, then, in such extremity.

bsb.text: Though an army encamps around me, my heart will not fear; though a war breaks out against me, I will keep my trust.

explanation.text: The secret of his confidence is his delight in communion with God (Psa 16:11; Psa 23:6), beholding the harmony of His perfections, and seeking His favor in His temple or palace; a term applicable to the tabernacle (compare Psa 5:7). There he is safe (Psa 31:21; Psa 61:5). The figure is changed in the last clause, but the sentiment is the same.

bsb.text: One thing I have asked of the LORD; this is what I desire: to dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to gaze on the beauty of the LORD and seek Him in His temple.
For in the day of trouble He will hide me in His shelter; He will conceal me under the cover of His tent; He will set me high upon a rock.

explanation.text: head be lifted up--I shall be placed beyond the reach of my enemies. Hence he avows his purpose of rendering joyful thank offerings.

bsb.text: Then my head will be held high above my enemies around me. At His tabernacle I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy; I will sing and make music to the LORD.

explanation.text:
Still pressing need extorts prayer for help.

cry with my voice--denotes earnestness. Other things equal, Christians in earnest pray audibly, even in secret.

bsb.text: Hear, O LORD, my voice when I call; be merciful and answer me.

explanation.text: The meaning is clear, though the construction in a literal translation is obscure. The English Version supplies the implied clause. To seek God's face is to seek His favor (Psa 105:4).

bsb.text: My heart said, “Seek His face.” Your face, O LORD, I will seek.

explanation.text: Hide not, etc.-- (Psa 4:6; Psa 22:24). Against rejection he pleads former mercy and love.

bsb.text: Hide not Your face from me, nor turn away Your servant in anger. You have been my helper; do not leave me or forsake me, O God of my salvation.

explanation.text: In the extremity of earthly destitution (Psa 31:11; Psa 38:11), God provides (compare Mat 25:35).

bsb.text: Though my father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.

explanation.text:
thy way--of providence.

a plain path-- (Psa 26:12).

enemies--literally, "watchers for my fall" (Psa 5:8).

bsb.text: Teach me Your way, O LORD, and lead me on a level path, because of my oppressors.

explanation.text:
will--literally, "soul," "desire" (Psa 35:25).

enemies--literally, "oppressors." Falsehood aids cruelty against him.

breathe out--as being filled with it (Act 9:1).

bsb.text: Do not hand me over to the will of my foes, for false witnesses rise up against me, breathing out violence.

explanation.text:
The strong emotion is indicated by the incomplete sentence, for which the English Version supplies a proper clause; or, omitting that, and rendering, "yet I believed," etc., the contrast of his faith and his danger is expressed.

to see--is to experience (Psa 22:17).

bsb.text: Still I am certain to see the goodness of the LORD in the land of the living.

explanation.text:
Wait, etc.--in confident expectation. The last clause is, literally, "and wait," etc., as if expecting new measures of help.

Next: Psalms Chapter 28

bsb.text: Wait patiently for the LORD; be strong and courageous. Wait patiently for the LORD!
